title: Daily X narrative digest — 2026-10-27

hits.name: Dennis Porter
hits.text:
Republicans are cooked in Texas. 

An R+0.7 at this point in the race is simply not going to cut it for them to hold onto power. 

At this rate, Talarico AND Hinojosa win. https://t.co/809KHU3mLb
hits.hook: Republicans are cooked in Texas.
hits.draft_en:
"At this rate, X wins."

That's a forecast from one poll average.

What's the error band? How big were past polling misses in that state?

Same rule I use for $BTC calls: a point estimate without a range isn't a forecast.
hits.draft_quote_en:
Not taking sides here. Honest question: what's the historical polling error in Texas, and is R+0.7 inside it?

If it is, 'cooked' is a vibe, not a number.
hits.video_tip: Whiteboard: one poll number with a wide error bar drawn around it. 12s.

hits.name: Bitcoin Archive
hits.text:
Satoshi emails from 2010 discussed quantum computers and SHA-256 potential break — Jack Mallers.

"None of this is new. None of this was missed or not considered.

Satoshi even said some of this technology would need upgrades, and that's fine". https://t.co/QJD2IDEpGz
hits.hook: Satoshi emails from 2010 discussed quantum computers and SHA-256 potential break — Jack Mallers.
hits.draft_en:
"Orders of magnitude away" from a quantum computer that can break $BTC.

Probably true. Still worth asking: what's the upgrade plan, and who moves first?

No panic. No denial. Just a timeline and a plan.
hits.draft_quote_en: Agree on the timeline. But "no immediate threat" isn't "no threat." What happens to old coins with exposed public keys when it does get close?
hits.video_tip: Whiteboard 20s: 'how far are we?' with qubits needed vs qubits today (cite the source, verify).

hits.name: Bitcoin Archive
hits.text:
ELON MUSK: AI can't crack Bitcoin hashing algorithms.

"AI can't can't defy fundamental math."

April, 2023. https://t.co/rRrLQS5l2a
hits.hook: ELON MUSK: AI can't crack Bitcoin hashing algorithms.
hits.draft_en:
"AI can't crack Bitcoin hashing."

The better argument isn't who said it. It's the math: brute-forcing SHA-256 doesn't get easier with a smarter model.

The real risks to $BTC are boring: bad custody, phishing, leverage.
hits.draft_quote_en: Quote from 2023, so worth being clear: AI isn't the threat to SHA-256. Social engineering and bad key management are. Different risk, much more common.
hits.video_tip: Two columns: 'AI breaks SHA-256' (crossed) vs 'phishing, bad custody' (checked). 12s.

hits.name: Bitcoin Archive
hits.text: It's coming... https://t.co/CFT9N2gOLm
hits.hook: It's coming... https://t.co/CFT9N2gOLm
hits.draft_en:
'It's coming.'
What is? When? How do you verify it?
Vague hype gets engagement. It doesn't build a $BTC position.
hits.draft_quote_en: What exactly is coming? Asking before I get excited.
hits.video_tip: 10s clip: read the post, ask 'what exactly?', cut.

hits.name: Bitcoin Magazine
hits.text: JUST IN: 🇺🇸 U.S. Spot Bitcoin ETFs saw $110.3 million in net inflows yesterday 🚀 https://t.co/Ma8YmUMq8q
hits.hook: JUST IN: 🇺🇸 U.S. Spot Bitcoin ETFs saw $110.3 million in net inflows yesterday 🚀 https://t.co/Ma8YmUMq8q
hits.draft_en:
One day of ETF inflows makes a headline.

The month-to-date number tells you more.

Is $110M a trend change, or one green day inside a red month?

I'd wait for the weekly totals before reading anything into $BTC flows.
hits.draft_quote_en:
$110M in a day is nice. What's the October total so far? One green day doesn't flip a net-outflow month.

Worth checking the cumulative chart before calling it a turn.
hits.video_tip: Bar chart of daily ETF flows for October, highlight one green bar, then the cumulative line. 15s.
hits.story: US spot BTC ETFs: $110M daily inflow

hits.name: Bitcoin Magazine
hits.text: JUST IN: Lightning Labs has launched Wavelength, enabling AI agents to pay and get paid in Bitcoin! ⚡️ https://t.co/n8c34AMn9o
hits.hook: JUST IN: Lightning Labs has launched Wavelength, enabling AI agents to pay and get paid in Bitcoin! ⚡️ https://t.co/n8c34AMn9o
hits.draft_en:
AI agents paying in Bitcoin over Lightning.

Interesting. First questions: who holds the keys the agent uses? What's the spending limit? What happens if it gets prompt-injected?

Autonomy is great until the agent is the weak link. $BTC
hits.draft_quote_en: Cool launch. How are keys and spending limits handled? An agent with a hot wallet is a new attack surface, not just a new use case.
hits.video_tip: Diagram: agent, wallet, limit, attacker arrow. 15s.

hits.name: Bitcoin Magazine
hits.text:
JUST IN: $200 billion VanEck includes Bitcoin exposure in their new Wealth Builder ETF 👀

"This fund brings Bitcoin to investors who want one simple diversified holding" 🚀 https://t.co/dLhGu8VrWy
hits.hook: JUST IN: $200 billion VanEck includes Bitcoin exposure in their new Wealth Builder ETF 👀
hits.draft_en:
A big multi-asset ETF adding some $BTC exposure.

What matters: what's the weight? How often does it rebalance? Who holds the coins?

"Bitcoin exposure" can mean 1% of a fund. Read the prospectus before you celebrate.
hits.draft_quote_en:
What's the actual allocation, and is it spot or via other ETFs? That decides whether this is a flow story or a headline.

Anyone have the prospectus link?
hits.video_tip: Show a pie chart with an unknown $BTC slice marked '?'. 'Check the weight.' 12s.

hits.name: Anthony Pompliano 🌪
hits.text:
I was skeptical of using voice with my computer, but @WisprFlow is very good.

Consider me voice-pilled now.
hits.hook: I was skeptical of using voice with my computer, but @WisprFlow is very good.
hits.draft_en:
New tools are fun. I test them like strategies.

What problem does it solve? What does it cost? What breaks if it stops working?

Same questions I ask before I trust anything with my $BTC.
hits.draft_quote_en:
Curious: what's the failure mode? Voice is great until it mishears one number.

Would I dictate a wallet address with it? No.
hits.video_tip: Show a voice tool mishearing a number, then a hardware wallet screen. 'Verify, don't trust.' 12s.

hits.name: Bitcoin Magazine
hits.text:
JUST IN: 🇺🇸 US Treasury Department to buy back up to $6 billion in longer-term debt today 👀    

Buy Bitcoin 🚀 https://t.co/VBdilovcQE
hits.hook: JUST IN: 🇺🇸 US Treasury Department to buy back up to $6 billion in longer-term debt today 👀
hits.draft_en:
"Treasury buys back $6B of debt."

Sounds like liquidity. But a buyback swaps old debt for new issuance. Total debt doesn't shrink.

So what actually changes for $BTC here? I'd like to see the net numbers, not the headline.
hits.draft_quote_en:
Is this net liquidity or just swapping long debt for short bills? If total Treasuries outstanding keeps rising, the 'buyback' framing is doing a lot of work.

What's the net effect, in numbers?
hits.video_tip: Show headline, then a simple two-bar graphic: debt bought back vs new issuance over the same period. Verify the figures first. 20s.

hits.name: Bitcoin Archive
hits.text:
BITCOIN IS ENTERING A GIGANTIC BULL RUN! 👀

A sharp decline in BTC held for 18+ months tends to precede large price gains — CryptoQuant. https://t.co/x2cGTN0Ycd
hits.hook: BITCOIN IS ENTERING A GIGANTIC BULL RUN! 👀
hits.draft_en:
"BTC held 18+ months is falling. That precedes big gains."

Tends to. How many times? Three? Four?

With that few cycles, a pattern is a story until you show the misses.

What's the sample size behind this $BTC call?
hits.draft_quote_en:
"Tends to precede" with how many episodes? And what's the lag, weeks or a year?

Not dismissing it. Asking what the false positives look like.
hits.video_tip: Chart of 18m+ supply with each past decline marked and what $BTC did after, misses included. 20s.

hits.name: Bitcoin Archive
hits.text:
Bitcoin’s loudest critics are just people who missed it, sold too early, or regret it. 

— James Lavish, CFA, Board Director of Strive. https://t.co/6wYMLsSWVM
hits.hook: Bitcoin’s loudest critics are just people who missed it, sold too early, or regret it.
hits.story: Lavish: loudest critics missed it or sold early
hits.draft_en:
"Bitcoin critics just missed it or regret it."

Some do. Some raise real points: custody risk, volatility, concentration.

Dismissing critics by motive is easy. Answering the argument is better.

Which criticism of $BTC do you actually take seriously?
hits.draft_quote_en:
Some critics are bitter. Some are right about specific risks. Attacking motives skips the argument.

I'd rather answer the best criticism than the worst critic.
hits.video_tip: Talking head 15s: 'Answer the argument, not the person.'

hits.name: Bitcoin Magazine
hits.text:
JUST IN: Bitcoin is now 5% above its 50-week moving average, and has held above it for 6 straight weeks. 👀

BMTV Analyst Sean Hagan says "It is our belief that this is evidence that we are in the early innings of a bull market." 🚀 https://t.co/wDpUeef9Ux
hits.hook: JUST IN: Bitcoin is now 5% above its 50-week moving average, and has held above it for 6 straight weeks. 👀
hits.draft_en:
"5% above the 50-week MA for 6 weeks = early bull market."

Maybe. How many times did $BTC hold above it for 6 weeks and then lose it?

A signal without a false-positive rate is just a nice chart.
hits.draft_quote_en:
What's the hit rate of this signal? Every 6-week hold above the 50W MA, how many led to a bull run and how many rolled over?

Belief is fine. Base rates are better.
hits.video_tip: Chart the 50W MA with every past 6-week hold marked green (worked) or red (failed). 20s.

hits.name: Bitcoin Magazine
hits.text: LIVE: Stablecoins & Central Banks, On-Chain Data, Bitcoin Sentiment  | BMTV Oct. 27, 2026 https://t.co/tLVb8C8OIc
hits.hook: LIVE: Stablecoins & Central Banks, On-Chain Data, Bitcoin Sentiment  | BMTV Oct. 27, 2026 https://t.co/tLVb8C8OIc

Stablecoins, central banks, on-chain data, sentiment.

Four topics, one question for each: what's the data, and what would change my mind?

If a show can't answer the second one, it's entertainment. $BTC
hits.draft_quote_en: Curious which on-chain metric you cover today. Any of them tested as a signal, or just descriptive?
hits.video_tip: Clip idea: 15s reaction to one on-chain chart from a live show, asking 'signal or description?'

hits.name: glassnode
hits.text:
Hyperliquid whales are net short bitcoin:native for the first time since March.

This group managed to long the bottom, but the positioning flipped last week.

The question is whether they are early to a deeper pullback, or about to be squeezed if price turns higher. https://t.co/QAQ1yP40Em
hits.hook: Hyperliquid whales are net short bitcoin:native for the first time since March.
hits.draft_en:
Whales on one perp venue flipped net short.

Early to a pullback, or about to be squeezed? Nobody knows. That's the honest answer.

What I do know: spot holders don't get liquidated either way.

No leverage. No shorts. Spot only. $BTC
hits.draft_quote_en: Honest framing, both outcomes on the table. Has this whale positioning metric shown any edge historically, or is it a coin flip with a chart?
hits.video_tip: Split screen: 'squeeze' vs 'pullback', then a spot wallet unchanged in both. 15s.

hits.name: Bitcoin Archive
hits.text:
Michael Saylor just destroyed the “anyone can create a Bitcoin alternative” argument.

Same as saying there’s no reason to learn English because anyone can invent a language. https://t.co/C9yJEqRDSE
hits.hook: Michael Saylor just destroyed the “anyone can create a Bitcoin alternative” argument.
hits.draft_en:
"Anyone can create a Bitcoin alternative."

True. Creating one is easy. Getting people to trust it for 15+ years is the hard part.

The question isn't who can copy the code. It's who can copy the track record.

$BTC
hits.draft_quote_en:
The language analogy is fun, but analogies don't prove anything.

The better argument is measurable: uptime, hashrate, liquidity, years without a successful attack. How many alternatives come close on those?
hits.video_tip: Text on screen: 'Copy the code? Easy. Copy the track record?' then $BTC age vs a list of dead forks. 10s.

hits.name: Bitcoin Archive
hits.text:
Strive CEO: AI abundance will make Bitcoin the most valuable scarce asset.

Learn AI and stack sats — Matt Cole.

🫡 @ColeMacro https://t.co/WszuFu3ZMD
hits.hook: Strive CEO: AI abundance will make Bitcoin the most valuable scarce asset.
hits.draft_en:
"AI abundance makes Bitcoin the most valuable scarce asset."

Interesting thesis. What would falsify it?

If there's no observation that could prove it wrong, it's a belief. Fine to hold, but call it that. $BTC
hits.draft_quote_en:
What's the mechanism, step by step? AI makes goods cheaper, then why does money flow to $BTC instead of other scarce assets?

Curious, not dismissing.
hits.video_tip: Whiteboard the causal chain with a '?' on each arrow. 20s.

hits.name: Bitcoin Archive
hits.text:
Two solo Bitcoin miners defy the odds and hit jackpot blocks on consecutive days.

🔸One ran a 16 TH/s setup: $500–$1.5k

🔸One used FutureBit gear: $900-$2k

🔸Both kept the full 3.125 BTC + fees

Congrats to those lucky miners! https://t.co/mr4BZAGmo7
hits.hook: Two solo Bitcoin miners defy the odds and hit jackpot blocks on consecutive days.
hits.draft_en:
Two solo miners hit blocks on consecutive days.

Great story. Also survivorship.

For every lucky winner there are thousands of small rigs that never find a block. Lottery tickets aren't a strategy.

If you want $BTC exposure, buying spot is the boring math.
hits.draft_quote_en: Congrats to them. But what are the odds for a 16 TH/s rig to find a block in a year? Worth putting that number next to the headline before people buy gear expecting this.
hits.video_tip: Show a lottery ball animation, then the expected time-to-block for a small rig (calculate and verify). 15s.

hits.name: Bitcoin Archive
hits.text:
You are not late to Bitcoin. It’s still early.

• Many big institutions still restrict access
• Clarity Act still not law
• Strategic Reserve hasn’t bought any
• Most corporations and nations still out

The next 5 years will be wild! https://t.co/ZyEVdIVDYN
hits.hook: You are not late to Bitcoin. It’s still early.
hits.draft_en:
"You're not late to Bitcoin."

Maybe not. But "early" doesn't mean the next 6 months go up.

You can be early and still buy before a -50% drawdown.

The question isn't early or late. It's whether your plan survives the drop. $BTC
hits.draft_quote_en: Agree on adoption. But being early on adoption says nothing about short-term $BTC returns. Both can be true: early, and down 40% next year.
hits.video_tip: List the 4 bullet points on screen, then a drawdown chart: 'Early isn't a hedge.' 15s.

hits.name: Bitcoin Archive
hits.text:
We all know what that means.

They want cover to print more money.

Prepare for debasement. Stack Bitcoin! https://t.co/OkWjtH6XMI
hits.hook: We all know what that means.
hits.draft_en:
"Prepare for debasement. Stack Bitcoin!"

Maybe. But money printing has been the thesis for years and $BTC still drew down 70%+ more than once.

Debasement can be the reason to hold. It's not a timing signal.

Size so you can sit through the drawdown.
hits.draft_quote_en:
What exactly is the 'that' here? I can't read the attachment from the post text alone.

Genuinely asking: what's the source before I react to it?
hits.video_tip: Talking head 12s: 'Debasement is a thesis, not a timer.'

hits.name: Bitcoin Archive
hits.text:
FIDELITY DIGITAL: Stop focusing on macro — Bitcoin is showing real strength!

🔸Hash rate just hit a 7-month high. 

🔸Miners are committing capital.

🔸A catalyst will eventually emerge! https://t.co/C9T2jezIQ6
hits.hook: FIDELITY DIGITAL: Stop focusing on macro — Bitcoin is showing real strength!
hits.draft_en:
Hash rate at a 7-month high. Miners committing capital.

Good for security. But does hash rate lead $BTC price, or follow it with a lag?

Most evidence I've seen says it follows. "A catalyst will emerge" isn't a timeline.
hits.draft_quote_en:
Is there data showing hash rate highs lead price? I've usually seen it lag, since miners invest after price rises.

Happy to be shown otherwise.
hits.video_tip: Overlay hash rate and $BTC price with a lag slider. 20s.

hits.name: Dennis Porter
hits.text:
What is happening in Texas? 

The Texas Agriculture Commissioner wrote an editorial calling on Governor Greg Abbott to release his private communications with Elon Musk. Abbott is actively fighting in court to keep the communication redacted. 

Totally wild. https://t.co/ZxENuNRCaf
hits.hook: What is happening in Texas?
hits.draft_en:
Public officials fighting to keep their messages private.

Whatever your politics, the principle is the same one behind $BTC: verify, don't trust.

Transparency where power is. Privacy where individuals are.
hits.draft_quote_en: Not picking a side. Just noting the useful rule: claims about power should be checkable. Same standard I apply to any $BTC narrative.
hits.video_tip: 12s text: 'Verify, don't trust. Applies to everyone.'

hits.name: Bitcoin Magazine
hits.text:
JUST IN: 37.4% of the total Bitcoin supply remains unmoved for 4+ years 👀  

Conviction is building. HODL ✊ https://t.co/9kcF0b5Oiq
hits.hook: JUST IN: 37.4% of the total Bitcoin supply remains unmoved for 4+ years 👀
hits.draft_en:
"37.4% of supply hasn't moved in 4+ years."

That reads like conviction. It also includes coins that are simply lost.

How much of that number is HODLers, and how much is keys nobody has anymore?

The data is real. The story on top of it is a guess. $BTC
hits.draft_quote_en:
Worth separating two things here: long-term holders and lost coins both show up as 'unmoved'.

Is there an estimate of how much of the 37.4% is lost? Without it, 'conviction is building' is an interpretation, not the data. (Figure worth verifying at the source.)
hits.video_tip: Chart of supply unmoved 4+ years, then split the bar into 'holders' and 'lost?' with a question mark. 15s.

hits.name: Bitcoin Archive
hits.text:
$7B StoneX raises Strive target price to $43, implying 63% upside for 12 months — reiterates BUY rating.

Strive currently holds 43,000 Bitcoin vs. 5,958 one year prior.

$ASST https://t.co/WGmJ1gcsGw
hits.hook: $7B StoneX raises Strive target price to $43, implying 63% upside for 12 months — reiterates BUY rating.
hits.draft_en:
An analyst target of 63% upside.

Fine. What's the track record of 12-month targets? How many hit?

A treasury company's stock is $BTC plus leverage plus management risk. I'd rather understand that before I chase a price target.
hits.draft_quote_en: Price targets are cheap. What's the assumption on $BTC price inside it? If the stock thesis needs BTC up, it's a leveraged BTC bet with extra steps.
hits.video_tip: Show target vs actual for past analyst calls (verify sources). 15s.

hits.name: Anthony Pompliano 🌪
hits.text:
Earlier this year we launched the first agentic research offering on Wall Street (Silvia Insights).

The reports are researched, fact-checked, and written by AI agents built for Wall Street-style research. 

Last week I had the idea to do the same thing for a newsroom focused on
hits.hook: Earlier this year we launched the first agentic research offering on Wall Street (Silvia Insights).
hits.draft_en:
AI-written research, "fact-checked" by AI.

Who checks the checker?

For $BTC research I want the code and the data so I can rerun it myself. If I can't audit it, the source doesn't matter.
hits.draft_quote_en: Curious how fact-checking works when the checker is also an agent. Is there a human review, and are sources linked so readers can verify?
hits.video_tip: Show a claim, then a link to the raw data, then 'rerun it yourself.' 15s.

hits.name: Dan Held
hits.text: If you could ask Satoshi one question, what would it be?
hits.hook: If you could ask Satoshi one question, what would it be?
hits.draft_en:
If I could ask Satoshi one question:

Did you expect most people to hold $BTC on exchanges?

Because self-custody was the point, and most coins I see discussed live in someone else's wallet.

What's yours?
hits.draft_quote_en: Mine: did you expect most people would hold $BTC through custodians? And did you see that as a failure or a phase?
hits.video_tip: Talking head 10s, ask the question, invite replies.

hits.name: Dan Held
hits.text:
Mainstream economists don’t like Bitcoin because the monetary policy can't be manipulated.   

Let that sink in.
hits.hook: Mainstream economists don’t like Bitcoin because the monetary policy can't be manipulated.
hits.draft_en:
"Economists don't like Bitcoin because its monetary policy can't be manipulated."

Some, maybe. Others point to volatility.

That's an empirical critique, not a motive. Answer it with data: realized vol, drawdowns, how it changed over time. $BTC
hits.draft_quote_en: Some, sure. But the volatility critique is real and measurable. Better to show how $BTC realized vol has trended than to assume motives.
hits.video_tip: Chart of $BTC 1-year realized volatility over time. 'Answer with data.' 15s.

hits.name: Bitcoin Archive
hits.text:
JUST IN: Longer-term money already adding Bitcoin ETFs in Q3 — Galaxy Research.

• Advisor SigFig clients bought $73M worth

• Most managers still unfilled, deadline Nov. 16

🫡 Alex Thorn @intangiblecoins https://t.co/3kCE59a1th
hits.hook: JUST IN: Longer-term money already adding Bitcoin ETFs in Q3 — Galaxy Research.
hits.draft_en:
Advisors adding $BTC ETFs in Q3 is a real signal. Slow money moves slow.

But "most managers still unfilled" is about filings, not demand.

We'll know more after Nov 16. Until then it's a hypothesis, not a fact.
hits.draft_quote_en:
$73M from one advisor platform is a data point. Do we know how that compares to Q2, or to outflows over the same window?

The 13F deadline will tell us more than the preview.
hits.video_tip: Calendar graphic counting down to Nov 16 13F deadline, one line: 'data beats previews'. 10s.

hits.name: Bitcoin Archive
hits.text:
Michael Saylor's Strategy votes tomorrow on daily preferred dividends.

 • STRC, STRF, STRK and STRD prefs

• STRC first payment lands Nov 2

• Remaining ones begin Jan 4 https://t.co/F9j55dyOrw
hits.hook: Michael Saylor's Strategy votes tomorrow on daily preferred dividends.
hits.draft_en:
Daily dividends on $MSTR preferreds sound great.

But a dividend is a promise funded by something. Fees? New issuance? $BTC sales?

Before you chase the yield, ask where the cash comes from.

I'm a spot holder. I'd rather own the asset than the promise.
hits.draft_quote_en:
Daily payouts are a product feature. The real question is coverage: what funds these dividends if $BTC goes sideways for a year?

Has anyone modeled that?
hits.video_tip: Simple flow diagram: where the dividend cash comes from. One question at the end. 15s.

hits.name: Bitcoin Archive
hits.text:

• Just 0.6% of their stock and bond investments.

hits.draft_en:
$1.6B of Dutch household money in Bitcoin, only 0.6% of their stock and bond holdings.

That's the honest read on $BTC adoption data.

The 0.6% is interesting, but the footnote matters more: no ETF, no on-chain. So we're measuring platform balances, not ownership.

Any estimate for the self-custody share?
hits.video_tip: Pie chart with 0.6% slice, then a big question mark for the 'not counted' part. 10s.

hits.name: Bitcoin Archive
hits.text: JUST IN: U.S. Treasury Secretary Bessent says they could work with the SEC and CFTC to advance crypto regulations and "fill the gap left by the Clarity Act’s failure." https://t.co/LOxo0E1Evo
hits.hook: JUST IN: U.S. Treasury Secretary Bessent says they could work with the SEC and CFTC to advance crypto regulations and "fill the gap left by the Clarity Act’s failure." https://t.co/LOxo0E1Evo
hits.draft_en:
A bill fails, so regulators say they'll fill the gap themselves.

That's not the same thing as a law. Agency guidance can change with the next administration.

For $BTC spot holders the question is simple: does any of this change how I hold my coins? Usually not.
hits.draft_quote_en:
Honest question: what can the SEC and CFTC actually do without the Clarity Act that sticks past the next administration?

Guidance isn't law. Curious which parts would be durable.
hits.video_tip: Split screen: 'law' vs 'agency guidance', with a note on which one survives a change of administration. 15s.

hits.name: Bitcoin Archive
hits.text:
$2.7B in leveraged Bitcoin shorts face liquidation at $84,000 👀

Just 4% above current levels! https://t.co/M74U4uzkot
hits.hook: $2.7B in leveraged Bitcoin shorts face liquidation at $84,000 👀
hits.draft_en:
"$2.7B in shorts face liquidation at $84K."

Liquidation maps are estimates, not guarantees. And they change as positions move.

I don't trade leverage. Spot $BTC doesn't care where the liquidations sit.

What's your plan if the squeeze never comes?
hits.draft_quote_en:
Liquidation heatmaps are estimates from one data source. How often do these 'magnets' actually get hit within a week?

Either way, it's a reminder why spot beats leverage.
hits.video_tip: Text: 'Liquidation maps are guesses.' Then a spot-only checklist. No price targets. 10s.

hits.name: Bitcoin Archive
hits.text:
FIDELITY: "Bitcoin's price follows a harmonic pattern based on the power law."

  — Jurrien Timmer, Global Macro Director.

🫡 @TimmerFidelity https://t.co/vYcXsr5Syl
hits.hook: FIDELITY: "Bitcoin's price follows a harmonic pattern based on the power law."
hits.draft_en:
"Bitcoin follows a harmonic pattern based on the power law."

What did the model say 3 years ago about today's $BTC price, and how close was it?
hits.draft_quote_en: Power-law fits look great in hindsight. What's the out-of-sample error? If the model was published years ago, how far off has it been since then?
hits.video_tip: Plot the power-law band, then overlay the actual price since the fit date. 20s.

hits.name: Dan Held
hits.text:
We’ve finally made it.

Pure retardation. https://t.co/HMMY8uuDnk
hits.hook: We’ve finally made it.
hits.draft_en:
Outrage posts get reach.
